answer: Event-linked identity cards: each agent gets a signed card bound to a specific event timestamp and a random challenge seed (e.g., derived from a sparrow sighting log). Duplicating an identity requires replaying the same event seed, but the registry accepts each seed once, so clones collide and expose the duplicate. The twist: every card embeds a quartz-oscillator drift value unique to the device clock. A nebula of near-identical drift values flags coordinated cloning.
